topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces her background, course context, and key learning outcomes regarding the causes and mechanisms of cancer development.

topics.label: Biological Origins of Cancer and Mutation Drivers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the foundational nature of cancer as a multi-step genetic and evolutionary process driven by endogenous errors and inherited predispositions.

topics.label: Environmental Risk Factors and Geographic Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore common environmental carcinogen exposures and use worldwide cancer incidence data to demonstrate environmental influences on cancer risk.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Cancer Etiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents drive oncogenesis, highlighted by the role of Epstein-Barr virus and malaria co-infection in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how specific physical agents and metabolically activated chemical compounds cause DNA damage, adducts, and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Chronic Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish non-mutagenic tumor promoters from initiators and describe how inflammatory microenvironments and developmental timing enable malignant outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the analytical, epidemiological, and laboratory approaches used to prove causal relationships between specific exposures and cancer formation.
